analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and file modes against the indexed model and selected detailed T-041 evidence. No concrete security regression is established in this scope. PlacementChecks/Main.swift:66 adds a Gemma check; lines 75–76 explicitly distinguish success from model execution or hardware qualification. PlacementChecks/run.sh:87–89 extends its compilation closure without changing execution privileges or cleanup. TensorParallelPlanChecks/gemma-run.sh:6–14 uses quoted paths, a fresh temporary directory and cleanup to compile and run local checks. GemmaTensorParallelPlanCheck.swift:39–89 checks tensor shapes, byte totals, rank cuts and refusal cases. Its unchecked argument and JSON casts can crash this local test executable, but no adversarial serving ingress is demonstrated. Derived 8-bit shapes are not independent evidence of an actual 8-bit artifact or inference correctness (T-007, T-027, T-056).
DistributedResidentExecution.swift's changed initializer delegates logprob support to ClusterModelFeaturePolicy.capturesLogprobs (head patch line 88), replacing the explicit tensor-mode adapter predicate. Existing base lines 373–381 reject unsupported logprobs and enforce request/context bounds. Integration must inspect the new policy and NativeWorkerRuntime behavior together to verify unknown adapters remain fail-closed and advertised capture matches actual execution and resource budgeting.
The libs/mlx-swift-lm gitlink changes at patch line 1, but dependency source changes are absent. Further review of that delta is material to TB-007, A-001, T-028 and T-041, including native request isolation, cache scoping and memory lifetime; the commit pointer alone proves neither a regression nor safety. No supplied change directly alters authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or cache persistence. Missing policy/dependency implementations remain coverage limits, not findings.
